suspicious_activity.narrative: Customer Cindy Clayton, with three active accounts opened between 2021 and 2023, engaged in multiple high-value cash withdrawals and deposits clustered on July 31 and August 1, 2025. Notably, on July 31, 2025, she made ATM withdrawals totaling $17,032.89 across three branches and a cash deposit of $5,500.55 at another branch. On August 1 and 2, 2025, additional large ATM withdrawals and cash deposits occurred. Several ATM withdrawals included named counterparties. This pattern of clustered high-value cash transactions across multiple locations is unusual and indicative of structuring to evade Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) reporting thresholds, constituting suspicious activity requiring filing under BSA regulations.
key_indicators: High-value cash withdrawals clustered on the same day across multiple locations
Large cash deposits in quick succession at different branches
suspicious_activity.ai_reasoning: Strong evidence of multiple high-value cash withdrawals and deposits clustered in short timeframes, including ATM withdrawals with named counterparties, aligns with structuring to avoid reporting thresholds. The presence of layering indicators supports money laundering but structuring is the primary pattern given the transaction clustering and cash focus.
